newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL outage wreaks havoc on crude markets.
newsitem.headline: IPL outage wreaks havoc on crude markets.

text.p: A shutdown of much of IPL Energy Inc's Interprovincial Pipe Line system to the United States from Canada was wreaking havoc in both upstream and downstream oil markets on Monday, traders said.
"As this shutdown continues to go on, every day it obviously gets more critical," a Calgary-based marketer said.
"It's caused phone calls flying back and forth between trading and the refineries to figure out their inventory positions and options. Guys are looking for anything."

A power outage in Minnesota late Saturday, as that state was battered by a freak spring snowstorm, knocked out three of IPL's pumping stations which took out about one million barrels of light, medium and heavy crude oil throughput.
The system was moving about 1.4 million barrels at the time. IPL said it did not believe the pumping stations could be back on line before Wednesday.

The outage forced a shutdown of lines 2, 3 and 13, which carry various crude grades to Superior, Wisconsin from Alberta, as well as Line 6 on the Lakehead system, which ships oil to the key Chicago refining market from Superior.

Traders said pipelines in Canada that deliver oil to IPL will show builds in inventory in the absence of a route out and if the situation continues for more than about three days, many producers will be forced to shut production in as their tanks fill to the lids.

Shippers were expected to try to make deliveries to the West Coast on BC Gas Inc's 250,000 barrel per day Trans Mountain Pipe Line and to the Rocky Mountain and southern Illinois regions the new Express Pipeline.
Express's first shipments of Canadian oil reached Casper, Wyoming only Saturday.

The 172,000 barrel per day pipeline, co-owned by Alberta Energy Co Ltd and TransCanada PipeLines Ltd, provides access to the southern Illinois refining market through the Platte pipeline system from the Rockies. Express officials could not immediately say whether the line or its tanks could handle the excess.

Trans Mountain manager of oil movement Rich Ballantyne said his firm had already received requests to provide storage for more Canadian oil. "The impact for us is that people want to bring in crude early and fill up our tanks to keep the production pipelines all running," Ballantyne said.

"It could have the effect of some more business our way, but we don't have an awful lot of spare capacity to begin with and IPL had some spare so I think they'll be trying to fill all their tanks up in Edmonton."
However, once IPL's tanks are full, feeder pipeline deliveries will have to be shut down, he said.

For refineries in southern Ontario, the immediate impact was minimal because Lakehead's Line 5, which runs to Sarnia, Ontario from Superior, was still shipping crude that was held in inventory, another Calgary-based trader said.
"But that's only for a day or so. I don't know how long they can keep running past maybe a day or or two days," the trader said.
Market players estimated that the Chicago market was short 250,000 barrels per day prompt-delivery light crude and 400,000 barrels per day of heavy oil.
"Guys downstream in Chicago are taking inventory of their position and this is going to be more of a prompt hit on deliveries because the line is shut down cold," the first source said.
"People are starting to make calls to find out if they can pull more barrels from the south, be it Gulf Coast barrels or WTI barrels."
